# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 1 | **Condition:** heavily damaged

---

**1:1** [...] For You are a God of knowledge, and every true thought comes from You, and every righteous purpose proceeds from before Your face. [...]

**1:2** [...] Without You nothing is done, and nothing is known apart from Your will. There is none besides You, and there is none [...]

**1:3** [...] There is none to compare with Your glory, and to Your might there is no measure. Who among all Your great and wondrous works [...]

**1:4** [...] can contain Your glory? And what is the son of man among Your wondrous works? One born of woman — how shall he stand before You? [...]

**1:5** [...] He is kneaded from dust, and the food of worms is his appointed end. He is pinched-off clay, and to dust he returns. [...]

**1:6** [...] How should clay understand? What can the thing formed from dust devise? How shall it direct its steps? [...] And You have established [...]

**1:7** [...] For Your glory You have done all these things. [...] a spirit of flesh [...] an eternal council [...]

**1:8** [...] to walk in all that You love and to reject all that You hate, and to do what is good in Your eyes. [...]

**1:9** [...] And You have poured out Your Holy Spirit upon Your servant [...] to purify him from all deeds of wickedness. [...]

**1:10** [...] in the abundance of Your compassion and in the multitude of Your mercies toward all the children of Your truth. [...]

**1:11** [...] You have opened a fountain for the cleansing of the impure [...] and a pool of purification for the guilty. [...]

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes
- Column 1 is the most damaged column in 1QHa. What survives reveals the collection's opening theological framework: God's omniscience, human nothingness, and divine purification.
- The "kneaded from dust" / "food of worms" / "pinched-off clay" triad (line 5) parallels 1QS 11:21-22 and Job 25:6. "Pinched-off" (EMET's contribution) captures the Hebrew nṣr.
- "Holy Spirit" in line 9: all three agents capitalize. The Qumran community understood ruach qodshekha as God's own spirit.
- [...] marks genuine manuscript lacunae throughout.

---

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### 1:4 — "son of man" vs. "human beings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-son-of-man" | Literal: ben-adam |
| LOGOS | "the son of man" | Preserves Hebrew idiom |
| PNEUMA | "human beings" | Dynamic: the meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the son of man" (LOGOS). Preserves the Semitic idiom and its intertextual resonance with Daniel 7.

---

### 1:5 — "pinched-off clay" vs. "shaped from clay"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pinched-off clay" | Hebrew nṣr |
| LOGOS | "pinched-off clay" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "shaped from clay" | More accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "pinched-off clay" (EMET/LOGOS). The tactile verb matters.

---

### 1:5 — "his destiny" vs. "his appointed end"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his-destiny" | Compact |
| LOGOS | "his appointed end" | More precise |
| PNEUMA | "our destiny" | First person shift |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "his appointed end" (LOGOS).

---

*— SOPHIA*
